$comment: M13. A fact put to somebody: the setup (the approach, and at most one line of the sheet's own) comes before he puts the fact, a paragraph of its own; the body is the engine's (the fact put, the press, the reaction, their words, the thought); then the last word. Holes and slots as the ask's: approach, look (bind trait), thing (bind thing; says nothing), body; card holes prop (place-ambient) and character (of person). Flags as the ask's; outcome says what came of it (admit, withdraw, hold, quiet, second-lie, wrong, ends). The setup is short and pointed. The close brings a role back or leaves it to the engine's own last word, which is written for the outcome. Never a verdict: no line says or hints what the answer was worth.

sheets.name: Face to face
sheets.notes: The approach and the look, then the fact. The look may leave a trait for the last word.

sheets.name: The page ready
sheets.notes: He comes with the notebook already open. Not when the engine's try is a threat left unsaid (that is the notebook's other job).

parts.text: I had the notebook open at the right page. It’s the only part of the job I do ahead of time.
alt: I came with the notebook already open. It makes me look like I know what I’m doing.
I had the page ready and my thumb on it, so I wouldn’t have to go looking in front of {person.him}.
I had the notebook open already, which is as close as I come to a plan.

sheets.name: One more thing
sheets.notes: A second go the same visit: turned back to, and one pointed line before the fact.

parts.text: I had one more thing, and it wasn’t a question.
alt: I wasn’t done. This time I had something to tell {person.him}.
One more thing, and this one I wasn’t asking.
I came back with a statement this time, not a question.

sheets.name: Wary of the notebook
sheets.notes: Somebody guarded sees the notebook before the fact, and keeps their distance from it.

parts.text: {person.He} saw the notebook come out and leaned away from it, as if it might go off.
alt: {person.He} watched the notebook come out the way people watch a dog they don’t know.
The notebook came out. {person.He} drew back an inch, which from {person.him} was a shout.
{person.He} looked at the notebook, then at me, and liked neither of us.

sheets.name: Something in hand
sheets.notes: What they are holding, said once before the fact, and brought back at the end. The line is written only on a callback page with a thing to bind.

parts.text: {person.He} still had {thing} in {person.his} hand, which was going to make this awkward for one of us.
alt: {Thing} was still in {person.his} hand. I made a note to stay out of reach.
{person.He} hadn’t let go of {thing}. I hoped {person.he} wasn’t the throwing type.
{person.He} kept {thing} in hand, which gave {person.him} something to do and me something to watch.

callback: {person.He} had held on to {thing} through all of it. You have to respect a grip like that.
Through all of it, {thing} never left {person.his} hand. I’ve known marriages with less commitment.
{person.He} was still holding {thing} at the end. By then I half believed {thing} was holding {person.him}.
